blocks.content:
Parliament can:
• Form a new state
• Increase or decrease area
• Alter boundaries
• Change names of states

IMPORTANT PROCEDURE:
1. Bill introduced only with prior recommendation of the President.
2. President refers the bill to the concerned State Legislature.
3. Parliament is NOT bound by the state’s opinion.
VERY IMPORTANT:
Simple majority is enough — NOT special majority.

rows: Referred to State Legislature, but Parliament is NOT bound

items: Prior recommendation of the President is mandatory before introducing the bill in Parliament.
Parliament is NOT bound by the views or opinions of the concerned State Legislature.
Special majority is NOT required for state reorganisation bills under Article 3; a simple majority is sufficient.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Parliament has the power to form new states, alter boundaries, change areas, and rename existing states.
A bill for forming or altering states can only be introduced with the prior recommendation of the President.
The President refers the bill to the concerned State Legislature for its views.
Parliament is not bound by the opinion expressed by the State Legislature.
Changes under Article 3 require only a simple majority, not a special majority.
